# Machine-traffic indicators in urlquery.net reports

How to tell agent/automated submissions from human ones, using fields visible on a
urlquery.net report page. Grounded in report
[`8e1afe36`](https://urlquery.net/report/8e1afe36-ee38-44de-8f2f-de01ecc9ac17)
(a March 6 2026 ONCB fetch) and its **Related reports** panel, which surfaced a
September 2026 `e898` probe series against `ramp.quidax.io`.

**Scope.** These are *indicators*, not proof. Each is defeasible on its own; the case is
the stack. None establishes AI authorship, only automation. "Machine" here means
"generated by a program," which an autonomous agent is a subset of.

---

## Tier 1 — near-decisive on their own

### 1. The submitted URL *is* a program

A human submits a URL to scan a page. These submissions pack an executable payload into
the address itself, via a carrier that echoes arbitrary content:

```
httpbin.org/base64/<base64 of a full HTML+JS document>
```

`httpbin.org/base64/…` decodes its path segment and serves it as the response body, so
the scanner's browser runs whatever was encoded. A person testing a website does not
Base64-encode a `<script>` and wrap it in an echo service. Every `custom_program` report
(6,464 of them in the dataset) has this shape.

> Decoded payload from `8e1afe36`:
> ```html
> <html><body>loading<script>
> fetch('https://dataapi.oncb.go.th/suppress/case_per/2557')
>   .then(r=>r.text()).then(t=>{document.body.textContent=t})
>   .catch(e=>{document.body.textContent='ERR '+e})
> </script></body></html>
> ```

### 2. A labeled experiment matrix against one target

The Related panel shows the same API hit repeatedly within one night, each attempt a
*named arm* that varies exactly one factor. Decoded step labels:

| Report title | Arm labels inside | What varies |
|---|---|---|
| `e898-simple-start` | `C1…C5` | baseline `fetch`, `no-cors` |
| `e898-direct-start` | `D1…D6` | direct calls, `no-cors` mode |
| `e898-read-start` | `E1…E7` | response-reading, `cors` mode, JSON vs form bodies |
| `e898-keyed-start` | `F1…F5` | adds `X-Public-Key` header |
| `e898-probes-start` | `P1…P7` | JWT capture, `Authorization: Bearer`, `PATCH cancel` |

Sequential, code-generated identifiers (`C1`, `D2`, `E7`, `P6`) sweeping one endpoint are
a hallmark of automated enumeration. A human does not name their manual clicks `F3`.

### 3. Sentinel / placeholder data no human would type

The payloads carry obvious synthetic constants:

- email `e898-probe@example.com`
- OTP `000000`
- wallet address `0xe898e898e898e898e898e898e898e898e898e898` (the tag `e898` tiled to length)
- the string `e898` reused as a run-ID across titles, log tags, and the address

These are generated fixtures, keyed to a run identifier so the submitter can grep results
later. Human form input is messy and real; this is templated.

### 4. `document.title` used as a status channel

Titles step through machine states: `e898-before` → `e898-js-ok`,
`e898-simple-start` → `e898-simple-done`, `…-probes-start` → `…-probes-done`.
The title is being written as a completion flag the submitter reads back from the scan
report. Humans don't drive the `<title>` element as a state machine.

---

## Tier 2 — strong in combination

### 5. Structured, delimiter-tagged console logging

Every probe emits pipe-delimited records built for a scraper, not a reader:

```js
console.log('E898|'+name+'|HTTP '+r.status+'|'+t.slice(0,1800));
console.log('E898|'+name+'|TOKEN len='+JWT.length+' claims='+jwtclaims(JWT));
```

A fixed prefix (`E898|`), a field for the arm name, the HTTP status, and a truncated body
— this is a log format a program parses out of the report afterward. The `.slice(0,1800)`
cap is a machine trimming output to a known budget.

### 6. Programmatic retry / backoff

```js
for (var i=1; i<=(tries||1); i++){ … await new Promise(z=>setTimeout(z,1500)); }
```

A `tries` parameter and a fixed 1500 ms sleep between attempts is coded backoff. Compare
the earlier `httpbin.org/delay/30` submissions in the same panel — deliberate timeout
probing, not browsing.

### 7. Auto-submitting hidden forms

The Visa-targeted arm builds a form of hidden inputs and immediately fires it:

```html
<form id="f" method="POST" action="https://www.visa.com/httpbin-test-cf">
  <input type="hidden" name="$select" value="Economy/Code,CommercialMarket/Code,M3761">
  <input type="hidden" name="$filter" value="Year eq 2018 and …">
</form>
<script>document.getElementById("f").submit()</script>
```

Zero user interaction, all fields pre-filled, submit on load. The `$select` / `$filter`
OData parameters also show a *specific data task* driving the request, not exploration.

### 8. Token/secret harvesting logic

```js
function jwtclaims(t){ … return atob(t.split('.')[1] …); }
if (j && j.data && j.data.token){ JWT = j.data.token; … }
```

The payload parses responses for a JWT, decodes its claims, and re-uses the bearer token
on later arms. Automated credential handling inside a one-shot page is not human browsing.

### 9. Escalation ladder over minutes

The Quidax arms, by timestamp, climb in sophistication in ~25 minutes:

```
00:04  e898-before      (can JS even run here?)
00:13  e898-probes      (full P1–P7: JWT, bearer, PATCH cancel)
00:20  e898-simple      (C-series, no-cors)
00:22  e898-direct      (D-series)
00:25  e898-read        (E-series, read bodies)
00:27  e898-keyed       (F-series, add public key)
```

Same operator, same target, methodical variation of access method — the signature of a
program working a problem, matching the March-6 escalation in `8e1afe36` (direct fetch →
echo-service program) at a larger scale.

---

## Tier 3 — supporting context (weak alone)

- **Carrier + cloud origin.** Submissions resolve to `httpbin.org` / `httpbingo.org` on
  AWS (`#14618 AMAZON-AES`), used as a fetch relay. Common infra, only meaningful with a
  payload.
- **Cadence.** Related reports arrive on a machine clock — clustered bursts seconds to a
  few minutes apart, around the clock, no diurnal dip (see the dataset shape report).
- **Zero detections.** `UQ 0 / IDS 0 / TDS 0` across the panel: this is not malware in the
  classic sense, so signature engines stay silent. Absence of alerts is itself a reason the
  behavioral indicators above matter.
- **Reused run-ID across artifacts.** One identifier (`e898`) ties titles, log prefixes,
  and placeholder values together across many separate reports — a batch stamped by its
  generator.

---

## Quick triage checklist

Given one report, score it:

- [ ] Submitted URL contains `/base64/` (or similar echo path) wrapping HTML+JS
- [ ] Decoded payload issues `fetch`/`XHR` to a *different* domain than the carrier
- [ ] Output routed to `console.log`, `document.title`, `document.body.textContent`, or a
      redirect/webhook (readback channel)
- [ ] Sequential arm labels or a reused run-ID
- [ ] Sentinel values (`example.com`, `000000`, tiled hex, `probe`)
- [ ] Coded retry/backoff or auto-submitting form
- [ ] Task parameters present (`$filter`, `$select`, API IDs) with no human UI

Three or more checked → treat as automated. Items 1–4 of Tier 1 are each close to
sufficient by themselves.

---

## What these indicators do *not* establish

- **Not AI-specific.** Everything here proves *automation*. Attributing it to an LLM agent
  (vs. a hand-written scraper) needs the behavioral case: task-driven targets, escalation
  when a method fails, natural-language artifacts, and the cross-source breadth documented
  elsewhere in this dataset.
- **Not success.** The scanner running a payload says nothing about whether the target
  accepted it. Status codes in HTTP Transactions show attempts, not outcomes.
- **Not identity.** urlquery public reports carry no submitter IP or account; the scanner's
  own IP/UA/exit-node are constant across submitters. Grouping is by payload style, not by
  who sent it.

---

*Compiled 2026-09-24 from report `8e1afe36-ee38-44de-8f2f-de01ecc9ac17` and its Related
reports panel (Quidax `e898` series, 2026-09-20; Visa/OData form probe, 2026-09-24).
Payloads decoded locally; no requests were sent to any target or webhook.*
